'''Katherine Jane Willis, Baroness Willis of Summertown''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|sep=,|size=100%|CBE|FRS}} (born 16 January 1964)<ref name="WW">{{Who's Who|year=2021|title=Willis, Prof. Katherine Jane|id=U274125|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U274125}}</ref> is a British biologist, academic and [[life peer]], who studies the relationship between long-term ecosystem dynamics and environmental change. She is Professor of [[Biodiversity]] in the [[Department of Biology, University of Oxford|Department of Biology]] and Pro-Vice-Chancellor<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.ox.ac.uk/about/organisation/university-officers | title=University Officers &#124; University of Oxford }}</ref> at the [[University of Oxford]],<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/people/katherine-willis | title=Professor Baroness Kathy Willis, CBE }}</ref> and an adjunct professor in biology at the [[University of Bergen]]. In 2018 she was elected Principal of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford|St Edmund Hall]], and took up the position from 1 October.<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor Kathy Willis elected new Principal of St Edmund Hall |url=https://www.zoo.ox.ac.uk/article/professor-kathy-willis-elected-new-principal-st-edmund-hall |publisher=University of Oxford Department of Zoology}}</ref> She held the Tasso Leventis Chair of Biodiversity at Oxford and was founding Director, now associate director, of the Biodiversity Institute Oxford.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biodiversity.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-katherine-willis/|title=Kathy Willis Profile at Biodiversity Institute|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150505183744/http://www.biodiversity.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-katherine-willis/|archive-date=5 May 2015}}</ref><ref>{{Scopus|id=7101793403}}</ref> Willis was Director of Science at the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] from 2013 to 2018.<ref name=kew>{{cite web|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140717110159/http://www.kew.org/science-conservation/plants-roots-to-riches/kathy-willis|title=Professor Kathy Willis, Director of Science|publisher=Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew|archive-date=17 July 2014|url=http://www.kew.org/science-conservation/plants-roots-to-riches/kathy-willis}}</ref> Her nomination by the [[House of Lords Appointments Commission]] as a [[crossbench]] [[life peer]] was announced on 17 May 2022. Willis was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in May 2026.<ref name=RS>{{cite web|url=https://royalsociety.org/news/2026/05/new-fellows-announcement-2026/|title=Exceptional scientists elected as Fellows of the Royal Society|date=27 May 2026|access-date=27 May 2026}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Katherine Jane Willis was born on 16 January 1964 in London to Edward George Willis and Winifred Ellen Willis ({{nee|Dymond}}).<ref name="WW"/> She gained an undergraduate degree in geography and environmental science from the [[University of Southampton]], and a [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[plant sciences]] from the [[University of Cambridge]] for research on the [[vegetation]]al history of the late [[Quaternary]] period in [[Epirus]], northwest Greece.<ref name=willisphd>{{cite thesis|degree=PhD|publisher=University of Cambridge|title=Late Quaternary vegetational history of Epirus, northwest Greece|url=http://idiscover.lib.cam.ac.uk/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=44CAM_ALMA21431220630003606&context=L&vid=44CAM_PROD&search_scope=SCOP_CAM_ALL&tab=cam_lib_coll&lang=en_US|website=lib.cam.ac.uk|first= Katherine Jane|last=Willis|date=1989|id={{EThOS|uk.bl.ethos.335183}}|oclc=556632964}}</ref>

==Career and research==
At the [[University of Cambridge]], Willis held a [[postdoctoral research]] fellowship at [[Selwyn College, Cambridge|Selwyn College]], a [[Natural Environment Research Council]] (NERC) postdoctoral fellowship in the Department of Plant Sciences, and a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] (URF) in the Godwin Institute for Quaternary Research. In 1999, she moved to a lectureship in the School of Geography and the Environment at the [[University of Oxford]], where she established the Oxford Long-term Ecology Laboratory in 2002.
Willis was made a professor of long-term ecology in 2008,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oxlel.zoo.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-katherine-willis/|title=Kathy Willis Oxford Long Term Ecology|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150519091654/http://oxlel.zoo.ox.ac.uk/people/professor-katherine-willis/|archive-date=19 May 2015|publisher=University of Oxford}}</ref> and in October 2010 became the first Tasso Leventis Professor of Biodiversity and director of the James Martin Biodiversity Institute in Zoology.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}} She was also an adjunct professor in the Department of Biology at the [[University of Bergen]], Norway.{{citation needed|date=July 2022}} She is a trustee of [[World Wide Fund for Nature|WWF-UK]],<ref>{{cite web|url=http://assets.wwf.org.uk/downloads/trustees_biographies_september2011.pdf|title=WWF-UK Trustees Biographies 2011|website=wwf.org.uk}}</ref> a panel member on the advisory board for the [[Commonwealth Scholarship Commission]], a trustee of the [[Percy Sladen Memorial Trust]], an international member on the [[Swedish Research Council]]'s FORMAS evaluation panel, and a college member of the UK [[Natural Environment Research Council]] (NERC).{{citation needed|date=July 2022}} From 2012 to 2013 she held the elected position of director-at-large of the International [[Biogeography]] Society.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.biogeography.org/html/About%20IBS/past_officers.html|title=International Biogeography Society, Past Officers|website=biogeography.org|access-date=23 January 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140201190346/http://www.biogeography.org/html/About%20IBS/past_officers.html|archive-date=1 February 2014}}</ref> In 2013, she was appointed Director of Science at the [[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]],<ref name=kew/> on a 5-year secondment from the University of Oxford.<ref>[http://www.kew.org/about-kew/press-media/press-releases-kew/new-director-of-science.htm Press Release, Kew Gardens]  {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140203010156/http://www.kew.org/about-kew/press-media/press-releases-kew/new-director-of-science.htm |date=3 February 2014 }}</ref> On 1 October 2018, Willis succeeded [[Keith Gull]] as Principal of [[St Edmund Hall, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seh.ox.ac.uk/news/st-edmund-hall-elects-new-principal|title=St Edmund Hall elects new Principal|website=St Edmund Hall}}</ref>

Willis's research<ref>{{cite web |url= https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Katherine_Willis2/|title=Data |website=researchgate.net}}</ref> focuses on reconstructing long term responses of [[ecosystem]]s to environmental change, including [[climate change]], [[Human impact on the environment|human impact]] and [[sea level rise]]. She argues that understanding long-term records of ecosystem change is essential for a proper understanding of future ecosystem responses. Many scientific studies are limited to short-term datasets that rarely span more than 40 to 50 years, although many larger organisms, including trees and large mammals, have an average generation time which exceeds this timescale. Short-term records therefore are unable to reconstruct natural variability over time, or the rates of migration as a result of environmental change. She also argues that a short-term approach gives a static view of ecosystems, and leads to the conceptual formation of an unrealistic "norm" which must be maintained or restored and protected. Her research group in the Oxford Long-term Ecology laboratory therefore attempts to reconstruct ecosystem responses to environmental change on timescales ranging from tens to millions of years, and the applications of long-term records in [[biodiversity]] conservation. She has argued that the impacts of contemporary climate change on plant biota is uncertain and potentially not as severe as researchers envision,<ref>University of Oxford. "Can Biodiversity Persist in the Face of Climate Change?." ScienceDaily. ScienceDaily, 14 December 2009. www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2009/11/091106111214.htm.</ref> and challenged assumptions made in the interpretation of spatially constrained temperature records.<ref>{{cite journal | last1 = Seddon | first1 = Alistair W.R. | last2 = Long | first2 = P. R. | last3 = Willis | first3 = K. | year = 2014 | title = Spatiotemporal patterns of warming | journal = Nature Climate Change | volume = 4 | issue = 10 | pages = 845–846 | doi = 10.1038/nclimate2372 | bibcode = 2014NatCC...4..845M | url = https://ora.ox.ac.uk/objects/uuid:16b6460e-ab7d-476d-b9ab-110068916dc4 }}</ref> Kew's ''State of the World's Plants'' report (2016) pinpoints land cover change as the major threat to global biodiversity, not climate change.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://stateoftheworldsplants.com/report/sotwp_2016.pdf |title=Archived copy |access-date=27 July 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160928190506/https://stateoftheworldsplants.com/report/sotwp_2016.pdf |archive-date=28 September 2016 }}</ref>

==House of Lords==
She was nominated as a [[life peer]] by the [[House of Lords Appointments Commission]] on 17 May 2022.<ref>{{cite web |title=Two new non-party-political peers – House of Lords Appointments Commission |url=https://lordsappointments.independent.gov.uk/wp-content/uploads/2022/05/HOLAC-PN-170522-1-1.pdf |website=House of Lords Appointments Commission |access-date=18 September 2022 |date=17 May 2022}}</ref> She was created '''''Baroness Willis of Summertown''''' on [[2022 Special Honours|8 July 2022]].<ref name="LG 12 July 2022">{{London Gazette |issue= 63756 |date= 12 July 2022 |page= 13218 |pages= |supp= |city= |title= |quote=}}</ref> Hers was the last peerage created by Elizabeth II. She made her [[maiden speech]] on 8 September 2022 during a debate on Climate Change and Biodiversity: Food Security.<ref>{{cite Hansard |jurisdiction= United Kingdom |url= https://hansard.parliament.uk/Lords/2022-09-08/debates/75D232A6-0CE8-4DF2-832A-8FB4B63616A9/details#contribution-6995A575-0CA5-465C-8CC7-2F38163400CC |title=Climate Change and Biodiversity: Food Security |house= House of Lords |date= 8 September 2022 |volume=824 |column_start= 342 |column_end= 345 |speaker= Baroness Willis of Summertown }}</ref> She sits as a non-party-political [[crossbench]] peer.<ref>{{cite web |title=Baroness Willis of Summertown: Parliamentary career |url=https://members.parliament.uk/member/4945/career |website=MPs and Lords |publisher=UK Parliament |access-date=18 September 2022}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Willis married [[Andrew Gant]], a composer and [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] politician,<ref>{{Who's Who|year=2019|title=Gant, Andrew John|id=U43512|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U43512}}</ref> in 1992. They have two sons and a daughter.<ref name="WW"/>
